newsitem.title: UK: C&W forges transatlantic cable deal with MFS.
newsitem.headline: C&W forges transatlantic cable deal with MFS.

text.p: British telecom company Cable and Wireless said on Monday it was linking up with U.S. telecoms group MFS Communication Co Inc to build and operated a transatlantic fibre-optic telecom cable system.
The company said in a statement that the system would be "the most advanced...yet constructed".

Cable and Wireless said it expected the system -- being built to meet the growth in demand for broadband services such as multi-media, Internet and other voice and data communications services -- to be in service in less than 15 months.

"The new transatlatic cable system will provide customers with resilient, diversely routed services between London and New York -- the two major telecommunications hubs for Americas and Europe," the company stated.

The venture will cost about 315 million stg to build. When it is complete, customers will for the first time be able to get competitively priced capacity from a single operator -- not just from coast to coast, but from London to New York, the firm said.
Cable and Wireless is completing oceanic survey work and will be the main marine installer for about 12,000 kms of Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH) looped cable system.

The main deal has been signed with Alcatel Submarine Networks, which will build the undersea portion of the cable system. The venture will be built using 10 gigabits capacity -- equivalent to about 125,000 simultaneous telephone calls.
Cable and Wireless said it would operate the system at the UK end under its existing licence, while MFS would land and operate the U.S. side.

Omaha-based MFS, a provider of communications services for businesses, which in August announced it planned to merge with U.S. telecom group WorldCom Inc, won a licence from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) earlier this month.
The two companies have applied to the FCC to be allowed to join forces and Cable and Wireless noted that other investors might take up minority interests in the system.

Cable & Wireless, which owns one twelfth of the world's undersea cable capacity, said the deal would reinforce its position as a major hub for European traffic and its ability to exploit international liberalisation -- especially in the trans-Atlantic market.
"Cable & Wireless descended from the company that laid the first-ever trans-Atlantic cable over 125 years ago," said Richard Brown, the group's chief executive.

"Cable & Wireless also built the modern era's first privately financed cable, PTAT, in 1989. We are proud, yet again, to play a breakthrough role in the development of the international cable market," he added.
